opening.headline: When you want to extract information from scanned PDFs and images, learn how input method, limits, and resolution affect accuracy and cost.
body: Let's say you have scanned receipts and contract PDFs piled up in a folder, and you need to structure and retrieve information such as dates, amounts, and items. With OCR, which extracts only letters, the structure of tables, stamps, and location information on charts are lost.

In this class, we take a look at how the three companies receive images and PDFs, the limits of PDF and document processing, the relationship between resolution and tokens, and things to keep in mind when dealing with multiple images. Next, we will check how to determine the input method in two cases: one receipt and a 100-page PDF.
opening.objectivesLead: By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:
objectives: Can explain image, PDF, and file input methods and limits
Distinguish the impact of resolution and page count on cost and accuracy

screens.title: I want to extract information from scanned PDFs and images.
screens.lead: Read about situations where you have a pile of documents to process. It is good to read while thinking about what is lost in the method of selecting only the letters.

visual.alt: A scene showing the location of the fields to be extracted on a scanned receipt image.
labels: Structure it and get it out

paragraphs: Scanned receipts and contract PDFs are piled up in a folder. What is needed is to retrieve information such as date, amount, and item as structured values. There is too much for one person to transcribe one by one.

What if we use OCR that only extracts letters? You get the letters, but the structure of the table cells, the location of the stamps, and the meaning of the charts are lost. If you don't know which column the number belongs to, you may misread the amount.

So we need a way to have the model read images and PDFs directly. What format should the file be sent in, what are the limits on size and page count, and how does resolution affect cost and accuracy? This is the question for this class.

callout.label: Things to think about
callout.text: Can I process a photo and a 100-page document in the same way? Check your answers in the two cases later in the lesson.

screens.outro: Before organizing the three companies' input methods into the same framework, let's first think about your own experience.

screens.title: think about it
screens.lead: When you select each question, the instructor's thoughts unfold. You won't have to enter or submit your answer, so think about it in your head first and then press it.

items.prompt: Have you ever experienced a broken table while converting a scanned document to text?
items.answer: In a table, the arrangement of columns, rather than each letter, creates meaning. If you move it to just text, this placement will be lost, making it difficult to know which number is the value of which item. This is why we need a way to view pages as images.

items.prompt: What would be different if you processed a photo and a 100-page document in the same way?
items.answer: You can send one page directly with your request, but 100 pages may be subject to request size and page limit. The delivery method also varies depending on whether you are asking a question once or multiple times.

items.prompt: Think about what information will be lost first if you lower the resolution.
items.answer: Small letters and numbers in tables are the first to become difficult to read. Large shapes or overall compositions remain even at low resolution. Depending on what you need to read, the resolution you need will vary.

screens.outro: I will organize it from three perspectives: input method, limit, and resolution. First is the input method.

screens.title: Multimodal input methods from three companies
screens.lead: Each row in the table represents how each company sends images and PDFs. Compare the names under which the same function is provided by each company.

data.caption: Image and document input method for each company
rows: The `image` block uses three methods: base64, URL, and file_id (Files API).
Write URL, base64, and file_id in the `document` block.
Input an image into the image understanding function. A token is assigned to each image and is adjusted with media_resolution.
Document comprehension is up to 50 MB or 1000 pages, and applies to both inline and Files API.
If you flip a non-PDF document in the same way, it will be treated as plain text.

Enter `input_image` in the Responses input and set `image_url` and `detail`. Images are provided in three ways: URL, Base64 data URL, and file ID from Files API. `detail` uses the value supported by the model among low, high, original, and auto. If omitted, it is auto.
This class does not cover OpenAI's PDF input method, but only compares the image input method.

The image formats in the API document are PNG, JPEG, WEBP, and non-animated GIF, and each request can be up to 512 MB in total. For reference, the ChatGPT app help guides PNG, JPEG, and non-animated GIF and 20MB per image.
data.notes: All three companies offer a method of putting it directly in the request and uploading and referencing the file first. What changes is the name and fields of the block, as well as the supported formats and limits. Even if the names are similar, the field configuration is different, so do not copy them as is. First check the application format in the documentation of the company you will be using. When sending the same image repeatedly, it is more advantageous to upload it and reference it rather than loading it directly.

screens.outro: Now that we've seen the input methods, let's look at PDF support and the limits of document processing.

screens.title: PDF support and document processing limitations
screens.lead: Let's take a step-by-step look at the limits you face when sending PDFs and how they are handled. Select the right arrow to check the items one by one.

visual.alt: The PDF goes through the request size limit, page limit, and token calculation in order.
labels: Upload to the file upload API and reference by file_id
Cut and send only the required range
Token calculation (Gemini is 258 tokens per side)

steps.title: 1. Two limits
steps.body: Claude's PDF support has a request size limit of 32MB (depending on platform), a maximum of 600 pages per request, and must be a standard PDF without passwords or encryption. For requests with context windows less than 1M, the maximum page count is reduced to 100. Note that limits vary depending on the model.

steps.title: 2. Limits apply to the entire request
steps.body: Both limits apply to the entire request, including other content sent along with the PDF. If there are question sentences or other attachments, you should not just count the PDF. Please configure it with some leeway in your limits. Configurations that operate near the limit may fail when the document grows even slightly.

steps.title: 3. Upload large PDFs for reference
steps.body: If you upload a large PDF to the Files API and reference it by file_id, the request size will be smaller. Files can be uploaded only once and reused in multiple requests, making them ideal for services that ask questions about the same document multiple times. Gemini also recommends the Files API for large files or documents to be used in multiple requests.

steps.title: 4. Gemini’s PDF Token Calculation
steps.body: Gemini counts one PDF page as 258 tokens. The document explains that large pages are reduced to a maximum of 3072x3072, and small pages are processed by enlarging them to 768x768. Making them smaller does not reduce costs, and processing them in larger sizes does not increase performance. In Gemini 3 and later models, the text embedded in the PDF is separately extracted and given to the model. There is no charge for this text token, and the page image token is counted as an IMAGE item. Since the number of pages determines the number of tokens, reducing the number of pages reduces the cost.

steps.title: 5. Non-PDF documents
steps.body: If you hand over a non-PDF document in the same way, Gemini will treat it as plain text. In this case, context such as charts or formatting is lost. If formatting is an important document, it is better to convert it to PDF and send it.

screens.outro: Next, we will look at the impact of resolution on cost and accuracy.

screens.title: Media Resolutions and Tokens
screens.lead: Use the slider to change the resolution and see how the tokens and readable information change.

visual.alt: Comparison illustration showing that as resolution increases, the token bars become longer and the number of readable elements increases.

stops.body: This is the setting that assigns the fewest maximum tokens to media. Costs and delays are reduced. It is suitable for scenes where you only need to view a simple background image or the overall composition. Keep in mind that lowering the resolution will make small text or table numbers more difficult to read.

It's the middle ground between quality and cost. In Gemini 3 and later models, the image is approximately 560 tokens. The Gemini document recommends medium for PDFs, and explains that in regular documents, setting it to high rarely improves character recognition. It is efficient to first try medium and upload only where read failures occur.

There are many tokens assigned so you can read small letters and numbers in tables. In Gemini 3 and later models, images are approximately 1,120 tokens, and high is recommended for image analysis. Ultra_high, which specifies item-only, spends approximately 2,240 tokens on the image and is geared toward special uses such as computer use. This is suitable for receipts with complex diagrams or small text, but adds tokens and costs.

Gemini's `media_resolution` balances quality, latency, and cost by setting the maximum number of tokens to allocate to media. The Gemini 4 and 3 models can provide different resolutions for each content item, allowing complex diagrams to be mixed at high and simple contextual images at low. Audio is tokenized at a fixed rate per second, regardless of resolution.

In Claude, images and PDF pages are counted as tokens and occupy the context window. In the Claude document, each 28x28 pixel piece of the image is one token, and the width and height are divided by 28 and rounded up to estimate the number of tokens. A 1000x1000 image is 36x36, so approximately 1,296 tokens. However, the maximum processing size and token upper limit vary depending on the model grade, and images exceeding the upper limit are reduced and processed. This formula is an estimate, so please check with the documentation of the model you are using and the token calculation function. PDFs cost approximately 1,500 to 3,000 tokens per page of text, plus the cost of page images. If you use the same image repeatedly, the cost burden will accumulate, so consider reusing the file by uploading it once using the Files API.

screens.outro: Let's continue with some things to keep in mind when dealing with multiple images.

screens.title: Things to keep in mind when understanding images and visuals
screens.lead: When you hover over or select an underlined term in the text, the impact appears as a speech bubble. Check them out one by one.

visual.alt: An example of requesting multiple images with a label such as 'Image 1:'.
labels: Compare the total amount of Image 1 and Image 2.

data.text: When multiple images are included in a single request, the model analyzes them together, and labeling them with identifiers such as "Image 1:" makes referencing easier. PDF support is based on vision functionality, so limits of vision applies directly. In Claude documents, there is a note stating that when using visual analysis via the Bedrock Converse path, Turn on quotation is required; otherwise, only text extraction is performed. The document provides an example where, depending on whether PDFs are extracted as text only or viewed as images in the same path, the token count of a three-page document changes to About 1,000 and about 7,000. This value is specific to that path and should not be directly applied to other paths. Images with the same screen configuration are reused and labeled as Upload only once with file_id.

terms.tip: This is an example of a label attached to multiple images. It's clear which image the question is referring to so the model doesn't get confused.
This limitation of image understanding also applies when reading PDF pages as images. Very small letters or blurry areas may be read incorrectly.
One caveat is that you need to turn on citations to write visual analysis on the Bedrock Converse route. You must check the requirements of the path you are writing.

This is an example showing the difference in tokens when only extracting text from a three-page document and when viewing the page as an image. Visual understanding improves accuracy, but may result in a significant increase in tokens.
When using the same image in multiple requests, upload it once to the Files API and reference it with an identifier, eliminating the burden of loading it in the body each time.

screens.outro: We will now explain the process of determining the input method using two business cases. First, a receipt.

screens.title: Description: One image of a receipt
screens.lead: The instructor determines the input method for processing a photo of a receipt. Select the right arrow to cycle through the input method, resolution, and output format decisions.

visual.alt: A decision flow that determines the transmission method, resolution, and output format for one receipt image.
labels: 1 Transmission method: base64 or directly as URL
If you ask multiple times, file_id
2 Resolution: Higher if the text is small

steps.title: 1. Examine the input
steps.body: The input is a photo of the receipt taken with a smartphone. It's just one page, and once you process it, you're done. These inputs do not require any complex configuration. Rather, making your configuration more complex than necessary only increases the points of failure.

steps.title: 2. Decide on the transmission method
steps.body: Since it is one sheet and written once, it is simple to send it directly as base64 or URL. It is rather cumbersome to go through the steps of uploading files separately. The shortest route is to send the image and question together in one request.

steps.title: 3. Decide on resolution
steps.body: Receipts have small text, so set the resolution to high. This is because small letters become difficult to read at low resolutions. If the background is complex, organizing it so that only the receipt is visible during the shooting stage will help with accuracy. The cheapest improvement is to clean up the input itself before resolving it with the model's settings.

steps.title: 4. Decide on the output format
steps.body: The extracted results are received as structured output in date, amount, and item fields. This allows you to put the results directly into the system and reduces formatting issues. Defining the amount as a numeric field and the date as a string field in date format makes subsequent verification easier.

steps.title: 5. Exception: Repeated Questions
steps.body: Only when I need to query the same receipt multiple times do I reuse the file_id by lifting it to the Files API. Please judge it separately from cases where it is processed once. Because the cost of repeat transmission disappears at the cost of increasing the number of upload steps, the number of questions becomes the standard.

screens.outro: This time, let's contrast it with an example of a long document.

screens.title: Commentary: 100 page PDF
screens.lead: The instructor determines how to handle a 100-page contract with a mix of tables and charts. Select the right arrow to follow the steps: check limits, upload, select range, and select processing method.

visual.alt: The flow includes checking the limit, uploading, selecting the range, and selecting the processing method for a 100-page PDF.
labels: 1 Check limits (request size, pages, 50MB and 1000 pages for Gemini)
2 Upload with Files API, reference by file_id
3 Select only the range of pages relevant to your question
4 Tables and charts are key for visual understanding, general text is for text

steps.title: 1. Examine the input
steps.body: The input is a 100-page contract PDF with a mix of tables and charts. Unlike receipts, they are large and the contents are not uniform. It's also possible to ask multiple questions on the same document.

steps.title: 2. Check the limit first
steps.body: Since you may be subject to the request size limit, first check whether the number of pages and size are within the limit. For Gemini, we look at whether it's within 50MB and 1000 pages, and for Claude, we look at the 32MB request size and 600 page limit (100 pages if the context window is less than 1M). Also note that the limits vary depending on the model.

steps.title: 3. Upload to Files API
steps.body: Large PDFs are uploaded to the Files API and referenced by file_id. Request sizes are smaller, and files can be reused across multiple questions.

steps.title: 4. Send only the necessary range
steps.body: If your question is only partially relevant, save tokens by truncating and sending only the required page range. For example, if the question asks about termination conditions, you only need to send the page with the termination provisions.

steps.title: 5. Distinguish between processing methods
steps.body: For those where tables and charts are the key, use visual understanding by looking at the page as an image, and for general text, distinguish whether text is sufficient. Visual comprehension increases tokens instead of increasing accuracy, as in the Bedrock Converse path where a three-page document varies from about 1,000 to about 7,000 tokens.

steps.title: 6. Differences between the two cases
steps.body: Direct transmission of receipts and high-resolution, structured output were sufficient. A 100-page PDF required checking limits, uploading, selecting a range, and categorizing processing methods. Even if the same model is used, the method will be different if the size of the input and the number of reuses are different. It is safe to first check the limit, then decide whether to raise it or send it directly, and finally decide what content to view visually.

screens.outro: Now let's summarize the entire lesson.

screens.title: The size, reuse, and content of input determine the method.
screens.lead: Let's go back to the first question and tie together the selection criteria for this class.

paragraphs: The first question was how to send images and PDFs to be read directly into the model. Images are sent using three methods: base64, URL, and file_id. PDFs also use the same three methods, and the Files API reduces the request size for large files.

PDF handles text and page images together and has request size and page limits. As the resolution increases, the number of tokens increases and the cost increases, so adjust it with settings such as media_resolution. Documents with charts and tables at their core require visual understanding, while simple text documents require text extraction.

Send a single page directly as an image, like a receipt, and upload a 100-page PDF to the Files API to select the pages you need. In either case, the way to protect both cost and accuracy is to first consider what resolution and page count are really necessary for accuracy.

There's a lot you can do in the input preparation phase. When shooting, you can clean up the background, crop the page to the required range, and upload the same file only once, increasing accuracy and reducing costs.

callout.label: something to remember
callout.text: The higher the resolution and number of pages, the better, but they are values determined according to the content to be read. Please also remember that limits apply to the entire request. A little tidying up in the steps of preparing your input will make all the steps that follow easier. For document types you are seeing for the first time, start with a small batch and check tokens and accuracy before expanding to the full scale.

glossary.def: In addition to text, inputs such as images, PDFs, and audio are also used.
This is an API that allows you to upload a file once and reuse it as an identifier.
This setting controls the maximum number of tokens that Gemini will assign to media.
This is a function that reads PDF text and visual information on the page together.
This method encodes binary data into text and places it in the request body.

misconceptions.myth: For PDF, just extracting the letters is enough.
misconceptions.fact: Charts and tables can lose meaning just by text extraction. For those where tables and charts are the key, it is necessary to have a visual understanding of the page as an image.
The higher the resolution, the more tokens and costs. It's better to only use small text or table numbers that need to be read.

misconceptions.myth: You can send it as long as the file size is correct.
misconceptions.fact: In addition to the request size limit, there is a maximum page count limit per request. Both limits apply to the entire request, so they should be viewed together.

closing.lead: Summarizes what was covered in this class.
points: Images are sent using three methods: base64, URL, and file_id. PDFs also use the same three methods. For large files, the Files API reduces the request size.
PDF handles text and page images together and has request size and page limits.
The higher the resolution, the more tokens the cost goes up, and this is adjusted with settings such as media_resolution.
Documents with charts and tables at their core require visual understanding, while text extraction is sufficient for simple text documents.
Like a receipt, a single page can be uploaded as an image, and a 100-page PDF can be uploaded using the Files API to handle the required pages.
